# GLM-5.3-Flash · RTX 3090 · NVMe streaming

A Dockerized local model server, reusing **Project Maya** (Strata-derived) and the exact **AJ-IQ2_XXS** quant linked in [this single-3090 recipe](https://x.com/ItsmeAjayKV/status/2111045102529593718).

## Hard constraint: weights must not exceed 100 GB

See **[SPEC.md](SPEC.md)**. The active model is **87,346,006,560 bytes** across two shards, pinned and SHA256-verified via `aj.lock.json`. The downloader, startup and benchmark automation reject manifests above **100,000,000,000 bytes total**, not per shard. Earlier 157 GB IQ4 and 125 GB EXL3 candidates are prohibited and stopped; their reports remain historical only.

AJ is a 2.23-bpw hand-mixed quantization, not a full-quality replacement for BF16. All routed experts remain; the unused MTP head is absent. Its model card reports a significant quantization-quality tradeoff. No expert skipping, LoRA, abliteration or runtime pruning is enabled here.

## Run

Linux, an NVIDIA RTX 3090 24 GiB, rootless Docker with NVIDIA CDI, Python 3, make, curl, and internal NVMe storage are required. This host has a Ryzen 5700G and 27.28 GiB usable RAM. Docker is capped at 24 GiB with container swap disabled. Leave room for ~87 GB weights, a small compatibility pack and the CUDA build/image.

```sh
make up                 # download+verify, build pinned Maya, pack once, start and wait
make test EXPERIMENT=validation-001
make status
make logs
make stop               # stays stopped, including across reboots
make start wait         # reuse the allowed model/container
```

The server uses **`--restart unless-stopped`**. Docker restarts crashes and resumes it after daemon/host restarts unless manually stopped. Rootless Docker itself must be enabled at boot; the user service and linger are already enabled here. A Docker unhealthy status alone does not restart a live process.

API: **http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1** · model **`glm-5.3-flash`** · default key **`local`**. Loopback binding is intentional. Use a private key and authenticated TLS proxy before exposing it remotely.

```sh
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer local' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"glm-5.3-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Why is the sky blue?"}],"stream":true,"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}'
```

Unlike the earlier llama.cpp template, Maya explicitly supports `enable_thinking=false`. Generation tests let answers finish naturally. Context is configured at 262,144 tokens; configured capacity is not itself proof of successful long-context retrieval.

## Settings and experiments

- Engine settings: `engines/maya.json` (context, prefill batch, 12 GiB RAM expert tier, worker count, GPU reserve). Run **`make recreate`** after changing them; existing containers retain their original arguments and file mounts.
- `make verify`: rehash both allowed weight shards.
- `make pack`: build upstream's required small BF16-compatible tensors and tokenizer. It does **not** duplicate/requantize all experts. A manifest marker makes this idempotent; `make maya-pack-force` refuses to rewrite a running server's pack.
- `make smoke EXPERIMENT=<unique-id>`: real model, authentication rejection, factual chat, SSE framing, multi-turn state and actual disk-read counters.
- `make restart-test EXPERIMENT=<unique-id>`: kill the API process, verify Docker recovery, verify explicit stop stays stopped, then start again.
- `make bench EXPERIMENT=<unique-id>`: long unique prompt and natural-end answer; records uncached prefill (prompt tokens / TTFT) and generation separately. `PROMPT_REPEATS=3200 PREFILL_ONLY=1` is a ~16K-token prefill probe with a naturally short factual answer; its decode rate is **not sustained throughput**.

**Commit and push settings before experiments.** The benchmark records the configuration Git hash, exact quant manifest, image ID, mounts, settings, token counts, cache policy, response, timings and outcome. Commit/push the JSON receipt and Markdown report after each run. Keep tests isolated from downloads/builds and other GPU workloads.

Reports: **[EXPERIMENTS.md](EXPERIMENTS.md)** · recipe/engine research: **[ENGINES.md](ENGINES.md)** · live operations memory: **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)**.

The target is **800–1000 tok/s uncached prefill**, not cached-prefix throughput. Only local measured results count. The reference post used a smaller quant and 46.7 GB pinned expert RAM; this host has less memory and a PCIe 3 NVMe/CPU platform. Results from different prompt sizes, quants, cache states or measurement methods are not direct speedup comparisons.

## Reused work

- [Project Maya](https://github.com/mw00/project-maya), Strata-derived GLM engine, pinned source `cd48762b6d4888205c130238dbc0c7f7904993cf` and ggml `3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d`, CUDA 12.8.1/sm_86. MIT license included in the container.
- [AJ-IQ2_XXS GGUF](https://huggingface.co/aj9o9/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF), revision `07c62fcdeaf1c05d22bd123c3da8058a1b1e63e2`; [original Z.ai model](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash), MIT.
- [0xSero/Sybil GLM NVMe recipe](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/glm-flash-lite): investigated its elastic cache, aligned O_DIRECT expert store and large-batch staging. Its pinned 3.05-bpw weights exceed the current size limit, so it is **not an allowed active candidate**.
- Earlier llama.cpp work: the unchanged MIT [xMytze/freedomljc expert-streaming patch](https://github.com/xMytze/glm53-ssd-streaming) remains in `vendor/` with its license/checksum for experiment provenance, not as the default deployment.

No model weights, logs, scratch research, caches or secrets are tracked in Git. No cloud fallback or invented performance numbers.

# GLM-5.3-Flash server specification

## CRITICAL — quantization size restriction

**Never download for use, load, serve, or benchmark a quantization whose total model weights exceed 100 GB.**

- **100 GB means 100,000,000,000 bytes**, summed across all weight shards/files of the model, not per shard and not just its active experts.
- Applies to every format and engine, including GGUF, EXL3, Strata/Maya, llama.cpp, and alternatives.
- No exception for CPU/NVMe offload, lower resident RAM, or faster benchmark results.
- Size must be checked against a pinned, hash-verified manifest before download or startup.
- Prior experiments with larger models remain historical records only. Those runtimes are stopped and must not be restarted.
- The 157 GB Unsloth IQ4_XS and 125 GB EXL3 candidates are **prohibited** under this requirement.
- The exact user-linked **AJ-IQ2_XXS** candidate is **87,346,006,560 bytes** across two shards and is within the limit. Its pinned manifest is `aj.lock.json`.
- Allowed Unsloth alternatives: **UD-IQ1_S =93,087,245,088 bytes** and **UD-IQ1_M =97,579,344,672 bytes** (pinned manifests `unsloth-iq1s.lock.json` / `unsloth-iq1m.lock.json`). Compatibility is assessed in ENGINES.md; neither is silently made the active model.
- Unsloth **UD-IQ2_XXS =101,844,951,904 bytes is prohibited**, even if a UI labels it 94.85 GiB. Do not confuse GB with GiB.

User imposed this restriction explicitly during implementation. Keep it in force across future sessions and experiments.

## Deployment and performance

- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash, locally served on this machine; reuse existing inference engines/recipes.
- Hardware: one RTX 3090 24 GiB, Ryzen 5700G, 27.28 GiB usable RAM, one NVMe SSD. Bound container RAM and disable container swap.
- Docker automation through Makefile; restart policy `unless-stopped`; keep the API loopback-bound by default.
- Prioritize uncached prefill. Target **800–1000 tok/s**, adapting the user's AJ-IQ2_XXS / Project Maya recipe; do not claim the target without local measurements.
- Reference context target: 256K. Validate memory fit, correctness and context independently of throughput.
- Run actual generation/SSE/lifecycle smoke tests. Record prefill and generation rates separately, including failures and short-sample caveats.
- Commit and push settings before experiments; record the exact configuration commit, quant manifest, settings, token counts, cache policy and metrics in JSON and Markdown; commit and push results afterward.
- Exclude weights, logs, caches, build artifacts, scratch research and secrets from Git.

# Engine investigation (2026-10-30)

**Latest hard constraint: no quant above 100,000,000,000 bytes total weights (SPEC.md).** The125GB EXL3 and157GB IQ4 entries below are historical investigation only; downloads/inference stopped and startup/packing are now blocked by size guards. Only87.35GB AJ-IQ2_XXS is an allowed active candidate.

## Exact user-linked AJ / Maya recipe (confirmed from the post)

Post: https://x.com/ItsmeAjayKV/status/2111045102529593718 (2026-10-16). Retrieved both the post and original screenshots, not inferred from a search snippet. It explicitly credits **Project Maya** and links **aj9o9/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF, AJ-IQ2_XXS**. This is distinct from the Sybil/0xSero EXL3 recipe below.

- Exact quant: **87,346,006,560 bytes**, two shards, 2.23 bpw, pinned HF revision `07c62fcdeaf1c05d22bd123c3da8058a1b1e63e2` in `aj.lock.json`. The earlier IQ4_XS test used ~157 GB, so it was not a reproduction of this post.
- Its dense/attention/shared weights are Q6_K, sensitive gates/indexer Q8_0, routers/norms F32, routed gate/up IQ2_XXS and down IQ2_XXS with higher precision on edge layers. All routed experts retained; unused MTP block removed by the quantizer.
- Screenshot: 863 tok/s prefill, 20.5 tok/s displayed decode, 7.7K/256K request context, 12.8 GB VRAM expert residency and **46.7 GB pinned RAM**, 48.3% VRAM hit rate; PCIe Gen4 x16, 12-core/24-thread CPU. Different memory residency than this host's ~12 GiB RAM tier and PCIe Gen3.
- Quality tradeoff is real: model card reports AJ-IQ2_XXS WikiText PPL 4.2314 vs BF16 2.2474 and KLD0.7072 (their 30-chunk experiment, not ours). Do not silently call it the same-quality model as IQ4_XS.
- Plan: reuse our working pinned Maya build, download+verify the exact AJ quant, build its own small compatibility pack, tune 16K/32K prefill batches and memory budget; target800–1000 but record only actual uncached measurements. Do not replace measured numbers with the post's claim.
- Storage priority: stop/resume EXL3 checkpoint preparation as needed; its separate117GB expert store must not crowd out this exact requested reproduction. Existing partial downloads remain resumable; never exceed disk free-space reserves.

## Unsloth alternatives below the hard limit

Pinned repository revision `a38483c8cd5df544f53d70fb281afe97369d5ab6`, checked via the HF blob API (not rounded UI sizes):

| Quant | Total shard bytes | Decimal GB | Allowed? |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| UD-IQ1_S | 93,087,245,088 | 93.087 | Yes; `unsloth-iq1s.lock.json` |
| UD-IQ1_M | 97,579,344,672 | 97.579 | Yes; `unsloth-iq1m.lock.json` |
| UD-IQ2_XXS | 101,844,951,904 | 101.845 | **No**, even though 94.85 GiB |

Header-only range reads of both data shards, parsed with upstream Maya's own `gguf_reader`, verified the actual routed-tensor formats (including the unused MTP head):

- IQ1_S: IQ3_XXS39, IQ2_XXS28, IQ1_S56, IQ4_XS3, Q3_K1, Q2_K2.
- IQ1_M: IQ3_XXS39, IQ2_XXS42, IQ1_M42, IQ4_XS3, Q3_K1, Q2_K2.

The pinned Maya build includes direct CUDA MMQ cases for IQ1_S, IQ2_XXS, IQ3_XXS, IQ4_XS, Q2_K and Q3_K. Its CPU native-expert tests explicitly cover the real UD-IQ1_S GLM geometry. **UD-IQ1_S is therefore the preferred Unsloth prefill candidate.** IQ1_M has decode support but no direct CUDA MMQ path in this build; those expert layers use a fallback, so a smaller bit label alone does not imply faster prefill.

These are source/header compatibility checks, **not successful inference or speed measurements**. Full weight downloads must be hash-verified and pack/model smoke tests must pass before adopting either. Finish the exact user-linked AJ quant first; avoid concurrent downloads during benchmarks. Neither Unsloth candidate is silently substituted for AJ in the active configuration.

## Located the single-3090 0xSero recipe

**[sybil-solutions/glm-flash-lite](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/glm-flash-lite)** (formerly `glm53-flash-offload`). This is the relevant GLM recipe, not the DGX Spark recipe found initially. Public Sybil code and `ghcr.io/0xsero` image lineage identify the connection. Source inspected at `6fe077da79a4d6fc842cf9f50cb703e4409924ca`.

Exact published NVMe image: `ghcr.io/sybil-solutions/glm53-flash-offload@sha256:aa74200f16c86588b101be2315aed2f643d148559179eef52a02599016b56e69` (v4.6-nvme). EXL3 3.05bpw weights at `turboderp/GLM-5.3-Flash-exl3`, revision `332ab457b709b7ba30dd9a448be5de03b80a7ac9`. Our `exl3.lock.json` pins content hashes, including dense/config/tokenizer files; no weights are committed.

### What makes it fast

- Prefill is an **8192-token GPU batch**, separate from decode, rather than small batches through a CPU expert compute path.
- A **117.3 GB aligned record store**, one 4 KiB-aligned record per complete expert. Deep O_DIRECT queue into pinned RAM; several-layer lookahead and overlapping NVMe reads, copy streams and GPU work.
- **Elastic VRAM expert cache**: lends up to 10 GiB back to prefill staging/activations; reclaims it for decode. No permanently reserved full expert layers starving large-batch prefill.
- Exclusive GPU/RAM expert residency avoids duplicate copies; a persistent host controller avoids per-layer host synchronization. A CPU lane handles RAM-resident decode misses.
- `nvme-exact` disables approximate CPU decode; prefill uses the exact EXL3 GPU path in either mode. "Exact" is relative to these EXL3 weights, **not BF16 equivalence**.

Published reference (not our measurements): 16 GiB cap, single RTX 3090, ~650 tok/s at 8K; ~1010 tok/s over a 93K prompt. **Reference host has EPYC 24 cores, eight RAM channels, PCIe 4 x16 and four Samsung 9100 PRO drives in RAID0 (~26 GB/s).** Our single PCIe 3 NVMe (~2.7 GB/s measured), 8-core two-channel host cannot inherit those numbers.

### Adaptation here

Reuse the published image unchanged; no new inference kernels. `engines/exl3.mk` automates pull/download/O_DIRECT probe/store packing+verification/start/wait/stop. 24 GiB no-swap cap, upstream small-host budget explicitly enabled, 1 GiB recurrent-state cache, 128 prefill-ring slots, CPU lane cores 2–7, feeder 0/controller 1/readers 8–15, 16 I/O threads. CDI + SELinux bind-mount settings match this rootless Docker host. No unlimited-memlock request (not permitted here; CUDA registration itself previously worked).

This host uses Btrfs, not upstream's recommended xfs/ext4. Its actual aligned O_DIRECT write/read probe passed on the store directory. The image's own probe and full packed-record verification must also pass before serving; **no filesystem repartitioning or loop devices**.

Preparation requires ~125.3 GB checkpoint +117.3 GB store plus image space; checked ~359 GiB free before starting. Keep the working GGUF engine as a fallback. Never run competing inference engines on the GPU during timing.

## Other engines worth testing

| Engine | Assessment / test plan |
|---|---|
| Current pinned llama.cpp streaming patch | Working and smoke-tested. Best recorded small-prompt result 7.80 prefill /1.41 gen tok/s at 460 prompt tokens; not an 8K-prefill comparison. Keep as exact GGUF baseline/fallback. |
| **Project Maya** (`mw00/project-maya`, Strata-derived) | High-value candidate: Linux-native, current GLM support, elastic expert tiers, large tensor-core prefill, 32 GB-class hosts. Can reuse existing GGUF or new EXL3, avoiding another weight download. Testing pinned source `cd48762b6d4888205c130238dbc0c7f7904993cf`, upstream ggml `3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d` in `engines/maya.Dockerfile`; sm_86, portable AVX2, existing GGUF with upstream's required BF16-compatible small-tensor pack. Explicit 12 GiB RAM tier, auto elastic prefill, no MTP, no skipping/LoRA/pruning. `engines/maya.mk` automates build/pack/start/wait. |
| `isichan-ai/Strata-GLM` | Reuses our exact Unsloth IQ4_XS; reported ~580 tok/s on 5090+128 GB. GLM path Linux explicitly untested, Windows-first packaging; less attractive than its actively maintained Maya lineage. Pin `6feb85fed9f994380b201c105851a740ec99d5e8` if tested. Disable expert skipping for fair quality. |
| `Indras-Mirror/Strata-GLM` | Linux support, but current defaults require ~80 GB free RAM, Maya-S-v2 weights and runtime abliteration/soft pruning. Do not adopt its defaults on this 27 GiB host or silently change model behavior. |
| `sergqwer/strata-glm` | Archived NVFP4 experiment (pin `ed37419fccd0c52e07d26d526a29c2098f547843`), 5090/128 GB/two NVMe, separate ~204 GB checkpoint. Poor first candidate here. |
| Current upstream `Niko1221/Strata` | Current README lists Qwen/DeepSeek, not GLM. Do not assume a Qwen engine can load GLM unchanged. Prefer a GLM-specific maintained fork/Maya. |

### Preparation checks

- Maya CUDA sm_86 build succeeded (152 compilation units). Initial pack attempt at configuration `d924430` stopped safely before serving: upstream's `_paths.py` requires `STRATA_GGUF_PY` explicitly even when the module imports via PYTHONPATH. Added that environment variable to the image; no inference happened, prefill/gen metrics N/A.
- EXL3 image pull and hash-verified checkpoint download run in parallel; disk/RAM monitored. Existing llama server explicitly stopped during engine transition, not crashed. No repartitioning or changes to the user's other workloads.

Results, failures, limits, configuration Git hashes and local prefill/gen rates go in `EXPERIMENTS.md`; remote claims above are only investigation context. A different quantization/runtime requires new correctness checks, not just a speed comparison.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measure real prefill/decode, preserve a receipt, append EXPERIMENTS.md."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import time
from smoke import MODEL, direct_io_files, io_stats, request
from wait import inspect


def git(*args):
    return subprocess.check_output(['git', *args], text=True).strip()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--id', required=True, help='Unique experiment label')
    parser.add_argument('--max-tokens', type=int, default=128)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not args.id.replace('-', '').replace('_', '').isalnum():
        raise ValueError('Experiment ID must be alphanumeric, hyphen or underscore')
    path = Path(f'results/experiment-{args.id}.json')
    if path.exists():
        raise RuntimeError(f'Receipt already exists: {path}; use a new experiment ID')
    commit = git('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
    if git('status', '--porcelain', '--untracked-files=no'):
        raise RuntimeError('Commit tracked configuration changes before benchmarking')
    state = inspect()
    command = state['Config']['Cmd'].copy()
    if '--api-key' in command:
        command[command.index('--api-key') + 1] = '<redacted>'
    direct = direct_io_files()
    prompt = ('Background notes (ignore this repetition): ' +
              'alpha beta gamma delta. ' * 80 +
              '\nWrite a detailed practical explanation of why the sky is blue. '
              'Use complete sentences and explain scattering, wavelengths, and sunsets. '
              'Continue for at least 300 words. Do not discuss the background notes.')
    payload = {'model': MODEL, 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': prompt}],
               'max_tokens': args.max_tokens, 'temperature': 0, 'seed': 42,
               'cache_prompt': False, 'chat_template_kwargs': {'reasoning_effort': 'low'}}
    before = io_stats()
    started = time.monotonic()
    with request('/v1/chat/completions', payload) as response:
        result = json.load(response)
    elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
    after = io_stats()
    timings = result['timings']
    usage = result['usage']
    final = inspect()
    valid = (usage['completion_tokens'] >= min(64, args.max_tokens) and
             timings['cache_n'] == 0 and timings['prompt_n'] > 256 and
             final['State']['Running'] and final['RestartCount'] == state['RestartCount'])
    resource = subprocess.check_output(['docker', 'stats', '--no-stream',
        '--format', '{{json .}}', state['Name'].lstrip('/')], text=True).strip()
    gpu = subprocess.check_output(['nvidia-smi', '--query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total',
                                   '--format=csv,noheader,nounits'], text=True).strip()
    receipt = {'id': args.id, 'tested_at': time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime()),
               'configuration_commit': commit, 'image_id': state['Image'], 'command': command,
               'environment': state['Config']['Env'], 'request': payload, 'response': result,
               'elapsed_s': elapsed, 'disk_read_bytes': after['read_bytes'] - before['read_bytes'],
               'direct_io_files': direct, 'docker_stats': json.loads(resource),
               'gpu_memory_used_total_mib': gpu, 'passed': valid}
    path.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + '\n')
    prefill = timings['prompt_per_second']
    decode = timings['predicted_per_second']
    report = (f'\n### {args.id} — {receipt["tested_at"]}\n\n'
              f'- Configuration commit: `{commit}`; receipt: [{path}]({path}).\n'
              f'- Settings: CPU_MOE={command[command.index("--n-cpu-moe") + 1]}, '
              f'cache={command[command.index("--moe-stream-cache") + 1]}, '
              f'batch/ubatch={command[command.index("--ubatch-size") + 1]}, '
              f'context={command[command.index("--ctx-size") + 1]}.\n'
              f'- **Prefill: {prefill:.2f} tok/s; generation: {decode:.2f} tok/s.** '
              f'New prompt={timings["prompt_n"]}, cached={timings["cache_n"]}, '
              f'generated={usage["completion_tokens"]}; wall={elapsed:.2f}s; '
              f'disk read={receipt["disk_read_bytes"] / 1e9:.2f} GB.\n'
              f'- RAM={receipt["docker_stats"]["MemUsage"]}; GPU used/total={gpu} MiB; '
              f'outcome={"PASS" if valid else "FAIL (inspect receipt)"}.\n')
    with Path('EXPERIMENTS.md').open('a') as stream:
        stream.write(report)
    print(report, flush=True)
    if not valid:
        raise RuntimeError('Benchmark failed validation; result still recorded')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resumable, hash-verified download from a pinned HF manifest (stdlib + curl)."""
import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess


MAX_MODEL_BYTES = 100_000_000_000  # CRITICAL user requirement: total quant, decimal GB


def validate_manifest(lock):
    total = sum(item['size'] for item in lock['files'])
    if total > MAX_MODEL_BYTES:
        raise ValueError(f'PROHIBITED quant: {total:,} bytes exceeds the 100 GB total-weight limit (SPEC.md)')
    if total <= 0:
        raise ValueError('Empty model manifest')
    return total


def sha256(path):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(8 * 1024 * 1024), b''):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def fetch(lock, item, dest, verify_only=False):

        if target.stat().st_size != item['size'] or sha256(target) != item['sha256']:

        raise RuntimeError(f'Missing shard: {target}')

    if partial.stat().st_size != item['size'] or sha256(partial) != item['sha256']:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Invalid downloaded shard: {partial}')
    partial.rename(target)
    print(f'Verified {target}', flush=True)


def main():

    parser.add_argument('--dest', type=Path, default=Path('models'))
    parser.add_argument('--lock', type=Path, default=Path('model.lock.json'))

"""Wait for this container, rejecting crash loops and stale listeners."""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request


def inspect():
    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['docker', 'inspect', os.getenv('CONTAINER', 'glm53-flash')]))[0]


def wait_ready(timeout=None):
    timeout = float(timeout or os.getenv('STARTUP_TIMEOUT', '1800'))
    name = os.getenv('CONTAINER', 'glm53-flash')
    url = f"http://{os.getenv('HOST', '127.0.0.1')}:{os.getenv('PORT', '8000')}/health"
    initial = inspect()['RestartCount']
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    print(f'Waiting for {name} at {url}', flush=True)
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        state = inspect()
        if not state['State']['Running'] or state['RestartCount'] != initial:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Container crashed: state={state['State']} restarts={state['RestartCount']}")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=3) as response:
                if json.load(response).get('status') == 'ok':
                    print('Server ready.', flush=True)
                    return
        except (OSError, ValueError, urllib.error.URLError):
            pass
        time.sleep(2)
    raise TimeoutError(f'API not ready within {timeout}s')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        wait_ready()
    except Exception:
        subprocess.run(['docker', 'logs', '--tail', '100', os.getenv('CONTAINER', 'glm53-flash')])

# GLM-5.3-Flash · RTX 3090 · NVMe streaming

A Dockerized local model server, reusing **Project Maya** (Strata-derived) and the exact **AJ-IQ2_XXS** quant linked in [this single-3090 recipe](https://x.com/ItsmeAjayKV/status/2111045102529593718).

## Hard constraint: weights must not exceed 100 GB

See **[SPEC.md](SPEC.md)**. The active model is **87,346,006,560 bytes** across two shards, pinned and SHA256-verified via `aj.lock.json`. The downloader, startup and benchmark automation reject manifests above **100,000,000,000 bytes total**, not per shard. Earlier 157 GB IQ4 and 125 GB EXL3 candidates are prohibited and stopped; their reports remain historical only.

AJ is a 2.23-bpw hand-mixed quantization, not a full-quality replacement for BF16. All routed experts remain; the unused MTP head is absent. Its model card reports a significant quantization-quality tradeoff. No expert skipping, LoRA, abliteration or runtime pruning is enabled here.

## Run

Linux, an NVIDIA RTX 3090 24 GiB, rootless Docker with NVIDIA CDI, Python 3, make, curl, and internal NVMe storage are required. This host has a Ryzen 5700G and 27.28 GiB usable RAM. Docker is capped at 24 GiB with container swap disabled. Leave room for ~87 GB weights, a small compatibility pack and the CUDA build/image.

```sh
make up                 # download+verify, build pinned Maya, pack once, start and wait
make test EXPERIMENT=validation-001
make status
make logs
make stop               # stays stopped, including across reboots
make start wait         # reuse the allowed model/container
```

The server uses **`--restart unless-stopped`**. Docker restarts crashes and resumes it after daemon/host restarts unless manually stopped. Rootless Docker itself must be enabled at boot; the user service and linger are already enabled here. A Docker unhealthy status alone does not restart a live process.

API: **http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1** · model **`glm-5.3-flash`** · default key **`local`**. Loopback binding is intentional. Use a private key and authenticated TLS proxy before exposing it remotely.

```sh
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer local' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"glm-5.3-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Why is the sky blue?"}],"stream":true,"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}'
```

Unlike the earlier llama.cpp template, Maya explicitly supports `enable_thinking=false`. Generation tests let answers finish naturally. Context is configured at 262,144 tokens; configured capacity is not itself proof of successful long-context retrieval.

## Settings and experiments

- Engine settings: `engines/maya.json` (context, prefill batch, 12 GiB RAM expert tier, worker count, GPU reserve). Run **`make recreate`** after changing them; existing containers retain their original arguments and file mounts.
- `make verify`: rehash both allowed weight shards.
- `make pack`: build upstream's required small BF16-compatible tensors and tokenizer. It does **not** duplicate/requantize all experts. A manifest marker makes this idempotent; `make maya-pack-force` refuses to rewrite a running server's pack.
- `make smoke EXPERIMENT=<unique-id>`: real model, authentication rejection, factual chat, SSE framing, multi-turn state and actual disk-read counters.
- `make restart-test EXPERIMENT=<unique-id>`: kill the API process, verify Docker recovery, verify explicit stop stays stopped, then start again.
- `make bench EXPERIMENT=<unique-id>`: long unique prompt and natural-end answer; records uncached prefill (prompt tokens / TTFT) and generation separately. `PROMPT_REPEATS=3200 PREFILL_ONLY=1` is a ~16K-token prefill probe with a naturally short factual answer; its decode rate is **not sustained throughput**.

**Commit and push settings before experiments.** The benchmark records the configuration Git hash, exact quant manifest, image ID, mounts, settings, token counts, cache policy, response, timings and outcome. Commit/push the JSON receipt and Markdown report after each run. Keep tests isolated from downloads/builds and other GPU workloads.

Reports: **[EXPERIMENTS.md](EXPERIMENTS.md)** · recipe/engine research: **[ENGINES.md](ENGINES.md)** · live operations memory: **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)**.

The target is **800–1000 tok/s uncached prefill**, not cached-prefix throughput. Only local measured results count. The reference post used a smaller quant and 46.7 GB pinned expert RAM; this host has less memory and a PCIe 3 NVMe/CPU platform. Results from different prompt sizes, quants, cache states or measurement methods are not direct speedup comparisons.

## Located the single-3090 0xSero recipe

**[sybil-solutions/glm-flash-lite](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/glm-flash-lite)** (formerly `glm53-flash-offload`). This is the relevant GLM recipe, not the DGX Spark recipe found initially. Public Sybil code and `ghcr.io/0xsero` image lineage identify the connection. Source inspected at `6fe077da79a4d6fc842cf9f50cb703e4409924ca`.

Exact published NVMe image: `ghcr.io/sybil-solutions/glm53-flash-offload@sha256:aa74200f16c86588b101be2315aed2f643d148559179eef52a02599016b56e69` (v4.6-nvme). Our `exl3.lock.json` pins content hashes, including dense/config/tokenizer files; no weights are committed.

### What makes it fast

- Prefill is an **8192-token GPU batch**, separate from decode, rather than small batches through a CPU expert compute path.
- A **117.3 GB aligned record store**, one 4 KiB-aligned record per complete expert. Deep O_DIRECT queue into pinned RAM; several-layer lookahead and overlapping NVMe reads, copy streams and GPU work.
- **Elastic VRAM expert cache**: lends up to 10 GiB back to prefill staging/activations; reclaims it for decode. No permanently reserved full expert layers starving large-batch prefill.
- Exclusive GPU/RAM expert residency avoids duplicate copies; a persistent host controller avoids per-layer host synchronization. A CPU lane handles RAM-resident decode misses.
- `nvme-exact` disables approximate CPU decode; prefill uses the exact EXL3 GPU path in either mode. "Exact" is relative to these EXL3 weights, **not BF16 equivalence**.

Published reference (not our measurements): 16 GiB cap, single RTX 3090, ~650 tok/s at 8K; ~1010 tok/s over a 93K prompt. **Reference host has EPYC 24 cores, eight RAM channels, PCIe 4 x16 and four Samsung 9100 PRO drives in RAID0 (~26 GB/s).** Our single PCIe 3 NVMe (~2.7 GB/s measured), 8-core two-channel host cannot inherit those numbers.

### Adaptation here

Reuse the published image unchanged; no new inference kernels. `engines/exl3.mk` automates pull/download/O_DIRECT probe/store packing+verification/start/wait/stop. 24 GiB no-swap cap, upstream small-host budget explicitly enabled, 1 GiB recurrent-state cache, 128 prefill-ring slots, CPU lane cores 2–7, feeder 0/controller 1/readers 8–15, 16 I/O threads. CDI + SELinux bind-mount settings match this rootless Docker host. No unlimited-memlock request (not permitted here; CUDA registration itself previously worked).

This host uses Btrfs, not upstream's recommended xfs/ext4. Its actual aligned O_DIRECT write/read probe passed on the store directory. The image's own probe and full packed-record verification must also pass before serving; **no filesystem repartitioning or loop devices**.

Preparation requires ~125.3 GB checkpoint +117.3 GB store plus image space; checked ~359 GiB free before starting. Keep the working GGUF engine as a fallback. Never run competing inference engines on the GPU during timing.

"""Resumable, hash-verified download from a pinned HF manifest (stdlib + curl)."""
import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess


MAX_MODEL_BYTES = 100_000_000_000  # CRITICAL user requirement: total quant, decimal GB


def validate_manifest(lock):
    total = sum(item['size'] for item in lock['files'])
    if total > MAX_MODEL_BYTES:
        raise ValueError(f'PROHIBITED quant: {total:,} bytes exceeds the 100 GB total-weight limit (SPEC.md)')
    if total <= 0:
        raise ValueError('Empty model manifest')
    return total


def sha256(path):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open('rb') as stream:
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(8 * 1024 * 1024), b''):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def fetch(lock, item, dest, verify_only=False):
    target = dest / Path(item['path']).name
    if target.exists():
        if target.stat().st_size != item['size'] or sha256(target) != item['sha256']:
            raise RuntimeError(f'Invalid existing shard: {target}; refusing to overwrite')
        print(f'Verified {target}', flush=True)
        return
    if verify_only:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Missing shard: {target}')
    partial = target.with_suffix(target.suffix + '.part')
    url = f"https://huggingface.co/{lock['repo']}/resolve/{lock['revision']}/{item['path']}"
    print(f'Downloading {target} ({item["size"]:,} bytes)', flush=True)
    subprocess.run(['curl', '--fail', '--location', '--silent', '--show-error',
                    '--retry', '12', '--retry-all-errors', '--retry-delay', '5',
                    '--connect-timeout', '30', '--speed-limit', '1024', '--speed-time', '120',
                    '--continue-at', '-', '--output', str(partial), url], check=True)
    if partial.stat().st_size != item['size'] or sha256(partial) != item['sha256']:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Invalid downloaded shard: {partial}')
    partial.rename(target)
    print(f'Verified {target}', flush=True)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--dest', type=Path, default=Path('models'))
    parser.add_argument('--lock', type=Path, default=Path('model.lock.json'))
    parser.add_argument('--verify', action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('--jobs', type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument('--check-only', action='store_true', help='Validate the hard size limit without downloading')
    parser.add_argument('--check-files', action='store_true', help='Validate the size limit and presence/size of all cached files')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    lock = json.loads(args.lock.read_text())
    validate_manifest(lock)
    if args.check_files:
        for item in lock['files']:
            target = args.dest / Path(item['path']).name
            if not target.is_file() or target.stat().st_size != item['size']:
                raise RuntimeError(f'Missing/incomplete weight file: {target}; run make download')
        print('All pinned weight files present, within the 100 GB total-weight limit')
        return
    if args.check_only:
        print('Manifest is within the 100 GB total-weight limit')
        return
    args.dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    needed = 0
    for item in lock['files']:
        target = args.dest / Path(item['path']).name
        partial = target.with_suffix(target.suffix + '.part')
        if not target.exists():
            needed += max(0, item['size'] - (partial.stat().st_size if partial.exists() else 0))
    if not args.verify and shutil.disk_usage(args.dest).free < needed + 10 * 1024**3:
        raise RuntimeError('Insufficient space: leave at least 10 GiB free after download')
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.jobs) as pool:
        list(pool.map(lambda item: fetch(lock, item, args.dest, args.verify), lock['files']))

## Why the Sky Is Blue

The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called **Rayleigh scattering**. As sunlight travels through the atmosphere, it collides with tiny gas molecules—mostly nitrogen and oxygen—that are far smaller than the wavelength of light itself. When light hits particles much smaller than its wavelength, each molecule scatters the light in all directions, and the intensity of that scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength (the Rayleigh law, ~1/λ⁴).

Because of this fourth-power dependence, shorter wavelengths are scattered far more strongly than longer ones. Blue light (around 450 nm) is scattered roughly five times more than red light (around 650 nm). So when you look up at the sky, you're seeing light that was redirected by the atmosphere toward your eyes rather than arriving directly from the sun. Blue dominates this diffuse light, which is why the sky reads as blue rather than violet—even though violet is scattered even more. The reason violet doesn't win is twofold: the sun emits less violet than blue, and our eyes are less sensitive to violet frequencies, so the combined effect peaks in blue.

At sunset and sunrise, the story changes. Sunlight must pass through a much longer slice of atmosphere when the sun sits low on the horizon—tens of times more air than at noon. The blue and violet components get scattered out of the direct beam along the way, leaving the longer wavelengths—orange and red—to reach the observer. That's why sunsets and sunrises glow red and orange: the red light, being least scattered, survives the long journey while the blue has been dispersed into the sky elsewhere (or into the twilight glow). Dust and aerosols can deepen these colors by adding additional scattering, which is why hazy or dusty evenings often produce the most vivid sunsets.
